cards.title: Two-band projector mismatch
cards.role: Defines the finite-momentum geometric event weight.

checks.reason: The source Hartree-Fock energy uses tr[P(k)P(k-q)] and explicitly expands this form factor.
Pauli trace identities give tr[P_k P_kq]=(1+n_k dot n_kq)/2.

cards.title: Small-q quantum-metric expansion

source_refs.value: Expanding up to a quadratic order

cards.latex: D(k,q)=q_i q_j g_ij(k)+O(|q|^3), g_ij=(1/4) partial_i n dot partial_j n
cards.role: Connects finite-momentum mismatch to the local quantum metric.

checks.reason: The paper's small-q expansion of the same form factor produces the Dirichlet energy.
Taylor expansion plus n dot partial_i n=0 yields the stated coefficient.

cards.numerical_form: Symmetrize over plus/minus q to remove odd corrections.

cards.title: Four-direction jump second moment

source_refs.value: Dirichlet energy is the integral of the trace

cards.latex: K_jump(q)=(2/q^2) integral_BZ Dbar(k,q) d^2k = integral_BZ tr(g) d^2k+O(q^2)
cards.role: Defines the calibrated isotropic probe whose topology can be bounded.

checks.reason: The source identifies the small-q density form factor with the integrated quantum metric/Dirichlet energy.
Averaging plus/minus x and y gives Dbar=q^2 tr(g)/2+O(q^4), fixing the prefactor 2/q^2.

cards.numerical_form: Periodic interpolation at four displacements followed by Brillouin-zone quadrature.
open_questions: A detector-specific bath kernel and unraveling are required before interpreting this calibrated weight as raw total click activity.

cards.title: Chern lower bound and Dirichlet normalization

checks.reason: The source states the trace inequality and E_D >= pi |C|.
The displayed projector definition gives E_D=(1/4) integral tr(partial_i P partial_i P)=K/2 for the standard metric g_ij=(1/2)tr(partial_i P partial_j P).

cards.numerical_form: Report both K/(2 pi |C|) and E_D/(pi |C|); the ratios are identical.
open_questions: The prose factor E_D=(1/4) integral tr(g) conflicts with the displayed projector formula and stated bound; this case uses the internally consistent convention.

cards.title: Massive Dirac texture and lattice Chern number
cards.latex: d=(sin k_x,sin k_y,M-cos k_x-cos k_y), n_0=-d/|d|, C=(1/4 pi) sum_triangles Omega_triangle
cards.role: Defines the paper's topological test texture and a gauge-free numerical invariant.

checks.reason: The main text specifies d(k), M=-0.5, n_0=-d/|d|, and C=1.
Oriented spherical-triangle areas discretize the degree and return zero for a constant texture.

cards.numerical_form: Two oriented triangles per periodic momentum plaquette.

cards.title: Small-q Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert flow
cards.latex: partial_t n=-n cross h+gamma n cross(n cross h), (2 pi)^2 h=2 lambda_T d-lambda_D laplacian(n)

checks.reason: Equation LLG equation and parameters gamma=1.5, lambda_D=1.25, lambda_T=0.025 are explicit in the main text.
Substituting P=(I+n dot sigma)/2 and [a dot sigma,b dot sigma]=2i(a cross b) dot sigma into the projector flow gives the printed precession and double-cross damping terms.
Both cross-product terms are perpendicular to n, so d|n|^2/dt=2 n dot partial_t n=0 before discretization.

cards.numerical_form: Periodic finite differences and RK4 with unit-vector projection.
open_questions: The source does not specify grid, step size, or integrator.

cards.title: Metriplectic Lyapunov inequality
cards.role: Defines the monotonicity acceptance check for the numerical flow.

checks.reason: The inequality is displayed as Eq. Lyapunov in the main text.
Cyclicity removes the Hamiltonian commutator contribution and turns the dissipative term into minus gamma times the Hilbert-Schmidt norm squared of the tangent projection.

cards.numerical_form: Check discrete energy increments against an integration tolerance and track topology separately.

cards.title: Paper bath is momentum-local
cards.latex: H_I=lambda sum_{k,alpha} c_k^dagger [b_{alpha,k}^dagger V_alpha(k)+b_{alpha,k} V_alpha^dagger(k)] c_k
cards.role: Fixes the actual Mera-Ozawa system-bath vertex and shows that it contains no transferred momentum q.

checks.reason: The published Supplemental Material writes the generic orbital vertex in Eq. (50) and its Bloch-band form in Eq. (103), with the same k on both fermion operators.
Reading the two fermion indices in the Bloch vertex gives c_k^dagger V(k)c_k; with no c_{k+q} term, its interband weight is same-k orbital rotation rather than the finite-q density overlap.

cards.numerical_form: Compare its same-k interband matrix elements with the finite-q density-probe form factor.
open_questions: The source derives an averaged one-particle flow, not a Lindblad generator or a detector unraveling.

cards.title: Paper Ohmic spectral superoperator and friction
cards.latex: J(omega,k)=sum_alpha delta(omega-Omega_alpha(k)) |V_alpha(k)><V_alpha(k)| approximately eta omega exp(-omega/omega_c) I_HS; gamma=2 pi eta lambda^2
cards.role: Separates the deterministic metriplectic damping coefficient from a physical click rate.

checks.reason: The supplement defines the matrix-space spectral density in Eq. (74), assumes an Ohmic identity superoperator in Eq. (76), and obtains gamma=2 pi eta lambda^2 after Eq. (85).
A sum of outer products |V_alpha><V_alpha| is a positive superoperator; replacing it by a positive Ohmic scalar times I_HS preserves positivity and yields a nonnegative damping coefficient.
The friction coefficient vanishes as lambda or eta tends to zero, recovering the Hamiltonian projector flow.

cards.numerical_form: Use an orthonormal Hilbert-Schmidt vertex basis to test what the identity superoperator can resolve.
open_questions: Bath occupation n_B appears in the assumptions but drops out of Eqs. (68)-(85), because the derivation evolves only the mean bath amplitude and omits noise correlations.

cards.title: Independent finite-q density probe
cards.latex: H_probe=lambda sum_q (b_q^dagger rho_q+b_q rho_-q), rho_q=sum_{k,m,n} F_mn(k,q) gamma_{m,k+q}^dagger gamma_{n,k}, F_mn=<u_m(k+q)|u_n(k)>
cards.role: Defines a detector-fixed spectator probe whose records contain the finite-q Bloch overlap.

checks.reason: The supplement's Eq. (29) gives rho_q=sum_{k,i} c^dagger_{k+q,i} c_{k,i}; changing to the instantaneous band basis gives F_mn.
Insert c_{k,i}=sum_n u_{n,i}(k) gamma_{n,k}; orbital completeness produces the stated overlap.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the band-basis form factor gauge-free as tr[P(k)(1-P(k+q))].
open_questions: This spectator probe is not the bath used to generate the Mera-Ozawa flow.

cards.title: Frequency-resolved calibrated click sum
cards.latex: R(q,omega)=2 pi lambda^2 J(q,omega) nu(omega) sum_k D(k,q) delta(omega-Delta_kq); A_cal(q)=integral d omega R/[2 pi lambda^2 J nu]=sum_k D(k,q)
cards.role: States exactly what must be energy resolved and calibrated before a click record becomes geometric.

checks.reason: The cited quantum-weight and topological-structure-factor papers identify the small-q density response with the static structure factor; the resolved detector kernel is the standard Fermi-golden-rule realization of that response.
Fermi's golden rule supplies the positive detector kernel and the squared density form factor for each resolved transition.
Dividing each resolved spectral bin by its nonzero kernel and integrating uses unoccupied-band completeness to return tr[P_k(1-P_kq)].

cards.numerical_form: Calibrate transition by transition; never divide an already integrated raw rate by a single average kernel.
open_questions: Kernel zeros and a finite detector energy window make the reconstruction incomplete.

cards.title: Conditional click-record topology bound
cards.latex: K_click(q)=2 Abar_cal(q)/q^2 -> integral_BZ tr(g) d^2k >= 2 pi |C|
cards.role: Gives the strongest valid version of the no-dark statement for a fixed scalar probe with full calibration.

checks.reason: Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 206602 establishes the Chern lower bound on the long-wavelength static structure factor; EQC003-EQC004 fix this case's normalization.
EQC011 reduces the calibrated record to EQC001; EQC002-EQC004 then give the small-q limit and Chern lower bound.

cards.numerical_form: Use four symmetric momenta and extrapolate linearly in q^2.
open_questions: The static quantum-weight/structure-factor bound is already established literature; novelty must come from time-resolved monitoring of the dissipative approach to saturation.

cards.title: Paper-bath complete-vertex response is texture blind
cards.latex: sum_a tr[Q V_a P V_a^dagger]=tr(Q) tr(P)=1 for rank(P)=rank(Q)=1
cards.role: Provides a decisive counterexample to reading quantum geometry from the paper's isotropic matrix-space bath.

checks.reason: Supplemental Eqs. (74), (76), and (104) explicitly replace the vertex sum by the identity superoperator in Hilbert-Schmidt matrix space.
For an orthonormal Hilbert-Schmidt basis, sum_a V_a X V_a^dagger=tr(X) I; tracing with Q gives the stated result.
The result is identical for a Chern texture and a constant trivial projector, so it cannot carry a Chern lower bound.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the four normalized Pauli-basis vertices pointwise for both topological and constant projectors.

cards.title: Raw-rate and orbital-vertex failure modes
cards.latex: R_raw proportional to lambda^2 J nu; R_raw -> 0 as lambda or nu -> 0, while D_M(k,0)=tr[P M^dagger (1-P) M] can be nonzero for M not proportional to I
cards.role: Shows why neither raw total activity nor an arbitrary orbital detector has a topology-only lower bound.

checks.reason: The detector-kernel dependence follows directly from the Fermi-golden-rule rate in EQC011, while the orbital vertex is the same general matrix structure used in Supplemental Eq. (50).
Golden-rule rates scale as lambda squared and thermal absorption vanishes when the incident occupation nu=n_B is zero.
At q=0 the scalar identity vertex gives P(1-P)=0, while a generic M rotates occupied weight into Q and leaves a nonzero constant term.

cards.numerical_form: Sweep lambda, temperature, detector window, and a non-scalar orbital vertex.

cards.title: Exact extended-Hubbard effective field
cards.latex: (2 pi)^2 h(k)=2 lambda_T d(k)-(1/pi^2) integral_BZ d^2q [U+2V(cos q_x+cos q_y)] n(k-q)
cards.role: Defines the exact finite-q evolution used for the paper's main Figs. 2 and 3.

checks.reason: The official Supplemental Material prints the interaction kernel, Hartree-Fock functional, two-band LLG equation, and the 1/pi^2 exact-field prefactor in Eqs. (117), (123)-(124), and (127)-(128).
Varying the symmetric double momentum integral produces two equal projector-overlap terms; the Pauli trace reduces them to the convolution with n(k-q).
Using cos(k_i-p_i)=cos(k_i)cos(p_i)+sin(k_i)sin(p_i) reduces the convolution exactly to five Fourier moments.
For a constant texture the cosine moments vanish, the interaction field is parallel to n, and the interaction-only torque is zero.

cards.numerical_form: Periodic quadrature of five vector Fourier moments followed by projected RK4.
open_questions: The paper does not disclose its momentum mesh, time step, or integrator.

cards.title: Small-q coupling for the extended Hubbard kernel
cards.role: Maps the exact interaction parameters to the comparison small-q flow.

checks.reason: Supplemental Eq. (131) prints the closed form after expanding v(q) through q squared.
Integrating q^3[(U+4V)-Vq^2] from zero to Q gives the printed Q^4/4 and Q^6/6 terms.
U=8, V=0.75, and Q=pi/2 give lambda_D=1.1828772769..., consistent with the paper's rounded 1.183.

cards.numerical_form: Direct scalar evaluation before running the approximate flow.

cards.title: Trace-condition deviation map
cards.role: Defines the momentum-resolved observable plotted in the paper's main Fig. 3.

checks.reason: The source figure's color-bar label explicitly uses one half of the trace-minus-absolute-curvature difference.
For P=(I+n dot sigma)/2, g_ij=(partial_i n dot partial_j n)/4 and F_12=-(n dot partial_x n cross partial_y n)/2.
The pointwise trace inequality makes Delta_tr nonnegative in the continuum; small negative samples are therefore a discretization diagnostic rather than physical data.

The supplement says energy and Chern use the same finite-mesh integration scheme but omits the stencil. Periodic spectral derivatives reproduce the reported near-pi energy, noninteger transition profile, and sharp T_short peak on one common mesh; centered differences and solid-angle Chern remain independent checks.

cards.numerical_form: Periodic spectral derivatives on a half-cell-shifted mesh for metric and curvature, with centered-difference and solid-angle diagnostics retained separately.
open_questions: The paper does not report the grid or its origin shift; N=141 and a half-cell shift are a convergence-backed reconstruction, not author metadata.
